content: Aquilegia vulgaris, commonly known as columbine, is a perennial herbaceous plant native to Europe. It typically grows to a height of 1 to 2 meters and features branched stems that are thinly covered with fine hairs. The leaves are pinnate in structure, with the basal leaflets further divided into three smaller leaflets. In traditional herbal medicine, columbine was regarded as a plant sacred to Venus, the Roman goddess of love. It was believed that carrying a small bouquet of columbine flowers could inspire romantic feelings in a loved one. The 17th-century herbalist Nicholas Culpeper recommended its use to alleviate the pain associated with childbirth. In contemporary herbal practices, the plant is utilized for its astringent and diuretic properties.
